finding_key: packages/backend/src/image/image.controller.ts::legacy `get /images/:id` is unauthenticated, and it is the endpoint the pptx/docx import path uploads to — imported deck images are world-readable
evidence: Verified against the supplied files: in `packages/backend/src/image/image.controller.ts`, `@Post()` and `@Delete(':id')` carry `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)` but `@Get(':id')` (line ~44) has no guard and no workspace scoping, while `packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts` guards with `CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard` and prefixes the S3 key with the workspace id. The upload chain the claim describes is also accurate: `slidesImageUploader` in `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts` delegates to `docsImageUploader`, which POSTs to `${BACKEND_BASE}/images` (the legacy, unprefixed route), so imported deck images land at bucket root and are readable via the unauthenticated GET. Two mitigations temper severity: keys are random UUIDv4 + extension (a capability URL, not brute-scannable in practice) and the design is explicitly relied upon elsewhere (`packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts` documents "Backend's `GET /images/:id` is publicly readable"), and the "workspace-scoped" wording in rest-api.md refers to the v1 endpoint, which genuinely is scoped — so that part of the prose overreaches. The behaviour is also entirely pre-existing and untouched by this diff, which only adds PPTX *export* (a read path).
